concerns.text: T003 requires computing 'AUC-ROC between `ss_score` and the binary label', but `ss_score` is a Semantic Similarity Score between the clean transcript and a DISTORTED ASR hypothesis — an artifact produced only by T004's distortion/ASR/SSS pipeline (`stress_curves.parquet`). T003 is ordered before T004, so its primary input does not exist when it runs. Either T003 must be split (power analysis + annotation collection before T004; AUC-ROC computation after T004), or T003 must move after T004. As written this is a consumer-before-producer violation.

concerns.location: tasks.md:Dependency table, T002 → T003 vs spec.md:FR-016
concerns.text: FR-016 states the human-validation gate 'is performed as a pre-study gate before US-1 execution', yet the dependency table orders T002 (US-1 data acquisition, FR-001) before T003 (the gate). The download of the ≥50,000-clip subset — the first US-1 execution step — runs before the gate that the spec requires to precede it. Reorder so the gate (or at minimum its power-analysis and annotation-protocol portions) precedes T002, or document why the gate is deferred.

T003 bundles three separable stages (power analysis, annotation tooling, AUC-ROC validation with FR-022 fallback) into one task whose inputs span both pre-data (G*Power) and post-ASR (ss_score) phases. Even after fixing the T004 dependency, the task as scoped cannot be executed as a single ordered unit; split it so each piece has a well-defined position in the dependency graph.
